MS George Eliot Will Be the World’s First Cruise Ship Dedicated to Solo Travelers
8 photos
Photo: Riviera Travel
The cruise industry is changing on multiple levels, including cleaner fuel alternatives, re-imagined layouts, and bold visions of year-long residencies. One of the most exciting trends caters entirely to solo travelers, those who are always disadvantages when it comes to conventional tourism and hospitality.
This ship named after a prominent literary figure isn’t brand-new, but it will herald a brand-new era, that of river cruises specifically tailored for folks traveling alone. This bold and welcomed initiative comes from Riviera Travel, an operator with more than 40 years of experience in the industry and a generous fleet of both river cruise ships and yachts.
Starting in 2027, the Riviera Travel MS George Eliot ship will start hosting solo cruises exclusively. Officially, it’s never been done before by a river cruise ship, and it sounds promising. The best part of this new concept is that guests can finally say goodbye to the dreaded solo supplements. Another great aspect is that they’re looking at a full season of what Riviera Travel calls “solo specific departures”, so there’s plenty to choose from.
A solo-exclusive river cruise ship also means that each guest gets to enjoy a double cabin all to themselves, and that alone makes these voyages a luxurious experience. Plus, it means that there’s more space onboard overall, in strong contrast to the over-crowded huge conventional cruise ships, and the staff to guest ratio is also automatically higher.
MS George Eliot is 110 meters long (360 feet), it was built by Scylla AG, one of the most acclaimed European builders of modern river cruise ships, and its re-imagined layout is meant to balance privacy with sociability. After all, solo traveling isn’t about isolation, but about personal comfort, as well as the opportunity to meet like-minded people.
Every one of the suites and cabins includes an en-suite bathroom with shower, individually-controlled air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a mini fridge, and other appliances (including a small coffee and tea station). There’s only one restaurant onboard, and it combines fine dining with informal free seating.
The Sun Deck is one of the most sought-after areas onboard MS George Eliot. It houses a splash pool, a putting green, sun loungers, and a shaded seating area. The Upper Deck houses the Riverview Kitchen, a boutique, and an observation lounge and bar. The Middle deck is all about dining – this is where guests go for delicious meals, from informal breakfasts to four-course dinners.
Riviera Travel operates both river cruise ships, which are long and low and adapted for cruising on European rivers, as well as motor yachts, specifically added for cruising the Adriatic and Dalmatian coasts. Solo trips are also available onboard the Riviera Travel yachts, and if you have been thinking about trying an European river cruise, this is the name to look for, as Riviera Travel specializes in European river cruises for American travelers.
